Kitty Killers

By: Liz Fish | Delivery

Proposal


Show:

Unique Selling Point:
Those sweet kitties who are social media darlings and have more YouTube and Instagram followers than most politicians are killing 30 million wild creatures a year on their midnight prowls. A recent paper released by SA National Biodiversity Institute (SANBI) and UCT has revealed that it’s not just happening on the urban edge of Table Mountain National Park, but right across Cape Town - 200,000 cats. Could well be far higher cause the kittycam batteries die after 2.30 and the cats hunt easily till 6.30am. Cat are a major contributor to the extinction of 26% of the worlds reptiles, mammals and birds and a threat to a further 25%

Summary:
Many cat owners believe their well-fed feline babies don’t kill and just lie around in the sun, but at night they go hunting, and GPS trackers show they can range as far as 3km from their homes. Those living on the edge of the Table Mountain National Park are killing off an astounding number of creatures, just one cat can kill up to 90,000 animals a year. They mostly kill reptiles and amphibians like the endangered Leopard Toad, but also birds and mice. They kill the reptiles, sometimes eating them, but cats like to play with their prey and so they will bring back an injured bird or mouse to play with at home.
Most studies to date have been done by surveys and it turns out that most owners are blissfully unaware of what their cats are up to at night. The UCT and SANBI study, which was conducted over the last 10 years, attached “Kittycams” to cats and monitored what they kill and how far they ranged. They discovered that 80% of the prey is never brought home.


Further information:
With an estimated 200 000 domestic cats in homes along the National Park border (and 300,000 in greater Cape Town), with a 3km range into the park, they are taking out the endangered Western Leopard Toad, the vulnerable Cape Rain Frog and the endemic Orange-breasted Sunbird. These animals are found nowhere else in the world, and all of them are being killed by cats. People say they keep cats to keep rats and mice at bay, but in fact cats’ prey is only 17% alien - they mostly kill endemic mammals, and reptile activity coincides with nocturnal cat hunting times, which means that species such as the Marble Leaf-toed Gecko were most popular.
With an estimated 300,000 cats in Cape Town, and each cat killing roughly 90 creatures a year it’s a lot of destruction. Feral cats- organization called Trap Neuter Release feeds 500 feral cats and neuter 3200. 330 times more domestic cats than wild cats like caracul We will have access to the footage from the kitty cameras and there some funny stories of kitties watching their owners in showers etc - but those have been censored!
This paper comes on the back of a slew of international studies from Australia, Northern Europe and America on how destructive domestic cats are. In Australia there 8 million feral and 2.5 million domestic cats which have contributed to the extinction of 28 indigenous Australian mammals. They are lethal killers and are a massive threat to indigenous biodiversity. Today they are flagged as one of the world’s 100 most invasive animals.
The results of the study have unsurprisingly caused a huge backlash from cat lovers. Cats are adored and have massive Instagram followings: like “Nala”, a tabby from the US with hypnotic azure eyes and 4.3-million Instagram followers. Similarly adored is “Tadar Sauce” for her dwarfism and underbite, @realgrumpycat had more than two-million Instagram followers, that’s more followers than politicians like presidential frontrunner, Joe Biden. They are important companions, especially under lockdown, but all that this paper is suggesting is a simple solution - just keep your cats indoors at night.
UCT is about to release another paper on how the residents of the Atlantic Beach Resort near Milnerton took CapeNature to court over a caracal (lynx) which was hunting their domestic cats and the authorities refuse to shoot the caracal, even after one cat was chased into its home and killed. It explores the very real issues around how to protect the wild mammals in the urban fringes from the growing urban sprawl.

Script:


Script: Cats are the world’s most popular pet, their beguiling beauty, playful natures and independence are oh so seductive, and which makes them addictive viewing
Link “Cats are social media darlings with more followers than some celebrities, so telling people that their fur babies are anything than exquisitely cute, is tough
Script: But when you switch off the lights they turn into fearless hunters, catching everything they can lay their paws on, from scorpions to bats, and their owners only see a fraction of what they’re killing.
Sam: Chase last week caught two creatures and probably in about three four days. He catches shrews moles, quite large mice , birds which is never that great.

Script: Sam Gouws lives on the edge of Table Mountain, with her family and two cats, which can disappear for days on end

Masa" Does it concern that they do that

Sam "it does concern me but at the same time I know it's natural and it's quite hard to take the natural instinct out of the animal.

Script: Although ornithologist Dr Rob Simmons always knew cats were hunters, it was a study conducted over 4 years tracking 130 cats, that revealed the extent of the carnage
Rob: Cape Town cats actually are reptile specialists a full 50 percent of all of the animals that were being eaten were reptiles. Especially marbled leaf toad geckos which cats love, they're a snack on wheels

Script: Knocking on over 400 doors across 22 suburbs, they worked out there are about 300 000 domestic cats in Cape Town, and their studies revealed that 60% hunt in summer, and 30% in winter

Rob “If you take all of Table Mountain National Park along the boundary, the perimeter we have got about 2200 cats the impact of those cats at 90 prey per year is just over 200 000 prey being taken from within this biosphere reserve, overall in Cape Town we're talking about 27 to 28 million animals being taken, that's just the domestic cats remember

Script: It was the two kitty-cam studies that were the game changer. Tracking 25 cats in 8 suburbs both in deep urban areas, as well as on the edge of Table Mountain, by UCT master’s student Frances Morling

Frances: we thought maybe cats were not actually bringing everything home to their families and maybe they were leaving things behind or eating it along the way. So we were really keen to try and pull back the curtain and find out what they were doing that it wasn't obvious to their owners.

Link: Cats spend most of their days curled up like this giving the impression that they are too well fed or lazy to hunt but the kittycams told a different story
Script: Teresa Thompson, one of the volunteers in the kittycam study was fascinated to discover the secret life of Daisy

Teresa " It was hysterical. We'd see again far off the road into neighbours houses. We just assumed they were around the house

Script: Each cat had two cameras which the owner swapped out and downloaded the footage, for 3 weeks.

Upsound

The grim part was freezing what the cat dragged in, for Frances to analyse, and as the batteries only lasted 2 hours, they were catching a whole lot more than was captured on camera

Teresa “She was an absolute predator. She would go off and come back with shrews mice once she came back with two little birds I think she must've taken them at the nest and loads of geckoes.

Script: It was like watching spycam footage, and there was over 700 hours of it. Initially it was quite difficult to work out, what they were watching. Nocturnal secrets of triumphant homecomings

to warding off the neighbourhood intruder, and remarkably only 18% of what they caught came home, the rest was eaten on the hunt, or abandoned.

Frances “We found is that one of the cats up a Newlands was actually it looks like friends with a porcupine. So they just came face to face in the dark and then just carried on with their lives which I thought was amazing

Teresa “ in the beginning we used to sit in front of the computer and look to see what she'd done it was all very exciting and we were careful what we did as a family because you've got a cat with a camera around its neck a…and I remember one day I was standing in the bathroom ….and I was just wearing a nightie and I looked down and Daisy was sitting on the floor between my legs looking up like this and I thought of goodness

Link “Cats were also fitted with GPS trackers and the study found that they were covering an area of 30 hectares in less than 2 weeks, now if you think about it that is pretty far into the reserve
Script: Koebraa Peters did the GPS study in winter, in Glencairn Heights, and really didn’t think cats would be so active

Koebraa “I never ever thought that domestic cats could have an impact on wildlife. 62 percent of the prey returns were reptiles, and these were mostly the marble leaf toed gecko so an endemic species or indigenous species. The other GPS study was done in summer, 44 percent of the prey composition consisted of small mammal species indigenous to the region

Script: And the cat owners were rather shocked, that their cats were crossing a busy road to hunt in the wetland.

Koebraa “What was really surprising was that one of the cats had caught and endemic and endangered Western leopard toad, they are toxic so generally cats and dogs will try and avoid them.

Script: People have cats to keep mice and rats at bay, but the study showed 80% of what cats are catching are indigenous species. The International Union for the Conservation of Nature have listed cats as the 100th most invasive species

Link: “Cats are actually an alien invasive animal they are responsible for wiping out 68 species globally and sadly in South Africa we just don’t know what they have already wiped out
Rob “There was a famous example the Stevens Island Wren was a flightless small bird. The lighthouse keepers cat his name was Tibbles. He cleaned up those flightless wrens in about two years and that bird is now extinct it is gone due to a domestic cat

Script: The UCT research corroborated studies done around the globe and they and all show the same thing, native wildlife is being hard hit

Rob” We asked the cat owners how often do you feed your or your cats and what is the prey return. There was no difference in the prey returned and how often they were fed, so a cat will hunt regardless of how hungry it is

Masa" Teresa does it bother you that cats kill 90 animals a year

Teresa" I wasn't aware of that. So I'm hoping that nature sorts itself out. So if the cat kills one or two shrews that you know the family is big enough to make up for that.

Rob” So if you're if you're saying cats are replacing the natural predators it's actually 300 times higher than the natural predator density of an equivalent of a caracul

Script: This study only looked at the impact of domestic cats, and no one has done a feral cat count. A kittycam study on feral cats in the USA, showed they catch 100 times more prey than domestic cats. If unspayed, cats can have 3 litters a year producing 18 kittens annually. Which is why the neuter programs are so critical, but this still doesn’t stop them from hunting, and they can live for 16 years

Masa ”Have you done anything to try and get your cats from stop hunting”

Sam ” the bells and the collars they remove I don't know how but they never really stay on. At nightime we do keep them inside or try keep them inside but there is a cat flap so they come and go quite a bit

Rob:” there are a lot of frustrated people around who are neighbours of cat owners I can tell you I have met a few of them, now that doesn’t have to be, the neighbour can enjoy their cat and the way you can get around that is so called catios, now catios are enclosed patios you even have tunnels out to the tree out to the garden, allows your cat to go out but it doesn't go roaming, it doesn't upset your neighbours doesn't go and catch the wildlife

Masa “Cats are adored globally, what was the reaction to the study”

Frances “ I had some death threats through Facebook which is something I hadn't experienced before. They think what we're trying to do is get rid of cats in neighbourhoods completely which is not true at all. And we just want people to be aware of the impact that their cats hunting can have so that people can take steps to be responsible and try and look after wildlife at the same time as enjoying having a cat

Script: Anneke Malan of Cats of South Africa, a collective of cat welfare organizations, raised her concerns about Carte Blanche's airing of the story on social media, before it was broadcast. We invited her to express her views on the study


Annette “ we are we are describing this study as irresponsible because we deal every day with cats being killed maimed by people and a study like this we fear is going to increase those numbers

Script: Cats of South Africa feed and rescue cats, and run trap, neuter, release programs. They fear the study will impact their work and are already struggling to raise funds for their rescue programs

Masa “But you not deny cats hunt and given access to wild areas they will hunt

Annette “ Oh definitely cats do hunt.

Masa “And if they are nera wildlife areas

Anneke “they will, but not nearly to the extent that is indicated in this study.
Script: Anneke's arguments were substantially based on those of a Research and Policy Analyst, of the Best Friends Animal Society, who challenges cat predation research. Dr Simmons informed us that he had already engaged Peter J Wolf, who didn’t reflect his feedback in his blogg. Simmons has yet to see a published study based on data, that undermines the UCT methodology and findings.
Anneke “Cats are the most persecuted animal on earth and they are just as necessary in food chain as any other creature”
Script” Dr Simmons reiterated that cat numbers are vastly out of balance with nature, and they think it would be irresponsible not to publish this data, given the mounting threats to wildlife on our planet.

metadata.Unique Selling Point: Those sweet kitties who are social media darlings and have more YouTube and Instagram followers than most politicians are killing 30 million wild creatures a year on their midnight prowls. A recent paper released by SA National Biodiversity Institute (SANBI) and UCT has revealed that it’s not just happening on the urban edge of Table Mountain National Park, but right across Cape Town - 200,000 cats. Could well be far higher cause the kittycam batteries die after 2.30 and the cats hunt easily till 6.30am. Cat are a major contributor to the extinction of 26% of the worlds reptiles, mammals and birds and a threat to a further 25%
metadata.Summary: Many cat owners believe their well-fed feline babies don’t kill and just lie around in the sun, but at night they go hunting, and GPS trackers show they can range as far as 3km from their homes. Those living on the edge of the Table Mountain National Park are killing off an astounding number of creatures, just one cat can kill up to 90,000 animals a year. They mostly kill reptiles and amphibians like the endangered Leopard Toad, but also birds and mice. They kill the reptiles, sometimes eating them, but cats like to play with their prey and so they will bring back an injured bird or mouse to play with at home. Most studies to date have been done by surveys and it turns out that most owners are blissfully unaware of what their cats are up to at night. The UCT and SANBI study, which was conducted over the last 10 years, attached “Kittycams” to cats and monitored what they kill and how far they ranged. They discovered that 80% of the prey is never brought home.
metadata.Further information: With an estimated 200 000 domestic cats in homes along the National Park border (and 300,000 in greater Cape Town), with a 3km range into the park, they are taking out the endangered Western Leopard Toad, the vulnerable Cape Rain Frog and the endemic Orange-breasted Sunbird. These animals are found nowhere else in the world, and all of them are being killed by cats. People say they keep cats to keep rats and mice at bay, but in fact cats’ prey is only 17% alien - they mostly kill endemic mammals, and reptile activity coincides with nocturnal cat hunting times, which means that species such as the Marble Leaf-toed Gecko were most popular. With an estimated 300,000 cats in Cape Town, and each cat killing roughly 90 creatures a year it’s a lot of destruction. Feral cats- organization called Trap Neuter Release feeds 500 feral cats and neuter 3200. 330 times more domestic cats than wild cats like caracul We will have access to the footage from the kitty cameras and there some funny stories of kitties watching their owners in showers etc - but those have been censored! This paper comes on the back of a slew of international studies from Australia, Northern Europe and America on how destructive domestic cats are. In Australia there 8 million feral and 2.5 million domestic cats which have contributed to the extinction of 28 indigenous Australian mammals. They are lethal killers and are a massive threat to indigenous biodiversity. Today they are flagged as one of the world’s 100 most invasive animals. The results of the study have unsurprisingly caused a huge backlash from cat lovers. Cats are adored and have massive Instagram followings: like “Nala”, a tabby from the US with hypnotic azure eyes and 4.3-million Instagram followers. Similarly adored is “Tadar Sauce” for her dwarfism and underbite, @realgrumpycat had more than two-million Instagram followers, that’s more followers than politicians like presidential frontrunner, Joe Biden. They are important companions, especially under lockdown, but all that this paper is suggesting is a simple solution - just keep your cats indoors at night. UCT is about to release another paper on how the residents of the Atlantic Beach Resort near Milnerton took CapeNature to court over a caracal (lynx) which was hunting their domestic cats and the authorities refuse to shoot the caracal, even after one cat was chased into its home and killed. It explores the very real issues around how to protect the wild mammals in the urban fringes from the growing urban sprawl.
